## (A) Surfaces in BiocCheck

### A1 — ERROR: `Remotes: github::timothy-barry/ondisc` {#a1}

Bioconductor (and CRAN) don't honour `Remotes:`. Every package in `Imports`/`Depends`/`Suggests` must be on CRAN or Bioconductor. The same gate also covers the eight `ondisc:::` calls in `sceptre` that reach into `ondisc`'s unexported internals — a `:::` usage that reviewers will flag separately.

**Resolution:** push `ondisc` back to CRAN with public wrappers for the entry points `sceptre` currently reaches via `:::`, then drop the `Remotes:` field. Gated on Tim's `ondisc` CRAN push.

### A2 — WARNING: No Bioconductor software dependencies {#a2}

`sceptre`'s `Imports` is entirely CRAN. Bioconductor reviewers may ask why submit to Bioc rather than CRAN.

**Resolution:** address with a cover-letter justification. The core argument: `sceptre`'s use of the `ondisc` data structure is better suited to the scale and access patterns of single-cell CRISPR screens than `SingleCellExperiment` — large sparse expression and gRNA-by-cell matrices with per-pair iteration, where on-disk-backed representation is essential. Kasper will back the argument. **Tim** to draft this section of the cover letter.

### A3 — NOTE: R version dependency 4.1 → 4.6.0 {#a3}

Bioconductor's policy is to require an R version no older than the current minor release minus one.

**Resolution — pending decision.** Recommend bumping `Depends: R (>= 4.1)` to `R (>= 4.6.0)`. Closes the NOTE; cost is locking out users on older R installs.

### A4 — NOTE: No `'fnd'` role in `Authors@R` {#a4}

If the work is supported by a grant, Bioconductor encourages crediting the funder via `person(role = "fnd")`.

**Resolution:** Wharton Analytics and U.S. National Science Foundation (Grants DMS-2113072 and DMS-2310654) added to `Authors@R` via the `fnd` role in [**PR #212**](https://github.com/Katsevich-Lab/sceptre/pull/212). Confirmed by `BiocCheck::BiocCheck()` on the PR branch: the "No 'fnd' role found in Authors@R" NOTE no longer fires.

### A5 — NOTE: `cat()` / `print()` outside `show()` methods (2 intentional sites) {#a5}

Two sites are intentional and remain after the previous cleanup pass:

- `R/s4_helpers.R:146` — inside a real S4 `show()` method. BiocCheck's parser cannot tell.
- `R/s4_analysis_functs_2.R:501` — inside a `sink()/print()/sink()` block that writes the analysis summary to disk.

Both are BiocCheck false positives in spirit.

**Resolution:** acknowledge in the submission cover letter; respond if a reviewer asks.

### A7 — NOTE: `\dontrun{}` / `\donttest{}` tags in man page examples {#a7}

3% of man pages — `man/sceptre-package.Rd`.

**Resolution:** acknowledge; rate is low. Reviewers rarely push.

### A10 — NOTE: Maintainer's Bioc-Devel mailing list subscription not verifiable {#a10}

`BiocCheck` cannot detect subscription — manual step required.

**Resolution:** Tim subscribes at <https://stat.ethz.ch/mailman/listinfo/bioc-devel> before submission.

## (B) Mentioned by Bioconductor documentation

### B1 — Version bump to `0.99.z` for first submission {#b1}

Bioconductor requires new packages to be at version `0.99.z`. Currently `0.10.3`.

**Resolution:** bump `Version:` in `DESCRIPTION` to `0.99.0` at submission time. Doing it earlier signals "submitting now" to anyone reading the repo, so postpone until the rest of the work is ready.

### B2 — `inst/scripts/` provenance for `inst/extdata/` data {#b2}

Bioconductor [docs](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/docs.html) require that `inst/extdata/` contents be accompanied by scripts in `inst/scripts/` documenting "how the data was obtained and prepared," including source URLs and pre-processing details. `sceptre` ships fixtures under `inst/extdata/{highmoi_example, parse_example}/` but currently has no `inst/scripts/`.

**Resolution:** add `inst/scripts/` with a provenance document for each fixture before submission.

## (C) Addressed anyway, with justification

### C1 — PR #205: option-aware `n_processors = "auto"` {#c1}

Two coupled changes:

- Make the `n_processors = "auto"` default honor the user's `parallelly.availableCores.fraction` R option (with `0.5` as the default when the option is unset). Previously, `parallelly::availableCores(fraction = 0.5)` was hardcoded, silently ignoring whatever the user had configured.
- Relax the `parallelly` version pin from `>= 1.47.0` to `>= 1.23.0`.

**Justification:** correct user-facing behavior. The hardcoded `0.5` had the surprising property of overriding a user's explicit `options(parallelly.availableCores.fraction = X)` setting, with no documented escape. Not BiocCheck-flagged; not in Bioconductor docs.

### C2 — PR #210: typo rename `fisher_yates_samlper` {#c2}

`src/generate_samples_functions.cpp:30` defined the C++ entry point with a typo (`samlper`). PR #210 renames the C++ symbol to `fisher_yates_sampler`, regenerates `RcppExports`, and adds an R-level `.Deprecated()` alias preserving the old name for any out-of-tree caller using it.

**Justification:** the typo is embarrassing, the rename is mechanical, and the deprecation alias keeps backward compatibility. Not BiocCheck-flagged; not in Bioconductor docs.

### C3 — PR #210: drop orphan `[[Rcpp::export]]` tags {#c3}

Nine functions across `src/check_functions.cpp`, `src/mixture_functs.cpp`, `src/shared_low_level_functions.cpp`, and `src/sparse_matrix_functs.cpp` carry `[[Rcpp::export]]` tags but have no R-side caller. PR #210 demotes them.

**Justification:** namespace hygiene; reduces surface area; avoids exporting C++ functions that aren't part of the user contract. Not BiocCheck-flagged; not in Bioconductor docs.

### C4 — PR #210: `using namespace Rcpp;` removed from header {#c4}

`src/shared_low_level_functions.h` had `using namespace Rcpp;` at file scope. PR #210 removes it and adds explicit `Rcpp::` qualification at use sites. `.cpp` files keep their `using namespace` — that's conventional.

**Justification:** `using namespace` at file scope in a header pollutes every source file that includes it. Standard C++ practice is to avoid this. Not BiocCheck-flagged; not in Bioconductor docs.

## (D) Deferred

### D1 — Function-length refactor (closes A6) {#d1}

27 functions exceed 50 lines. Refactoring is high-touch and risks introducing regressions in well-tested code.

**Decision:** deferred. Submit as-is; BiocCheck NOTEs do not block submission. Revisit post-acceptance if useful.

### D2 — Whitespace styler pass (closes A8, A9) {#d2}

`styler::style_pkg()` would close the line-length and indent NOTEs but produces a massive whitespace-only diff that obscures `git blame` and conflicts with concurrent feature work.

**Decision:** deferred. Single-shot pass after the submission lands.

### D3 — `setValidity()` for `sceptre_object` {#d3}

A common reviewer-pushback item on packages with user-facing S4 classes.

**Decision:** declined. `sceptre_object` is built incrementally across the pipeline (`import_data` → `set_analysis_parameters` → `assign_grnas` → `run_qc` → …), so many slots are legitimately empty at intermediate stages. A stage-independent validity method catches few real bugs for its maintenance cost; a stage-aware one would require explicit `validObject()` calls through the function chain. The class is not exported in `NAMESPACE`. Revisit if a reviewer asks.

### D4 — Class-level documentation for `sceptre_object` {#d4}

A `man/sceptre_object-class.Rd` enumerating each slot.

**Decision:** declined. `sceptre_object` is not exported. The sceptre book directs users to accessor functions (`get_response_matrix()`, `get_grna_matrix()`, `get_cell_covariates()`) rather than slots; `?sceptre_object` returning no help page is consistent with that user contract. R CMD check does not flag missing documentation on unexported S4 classes. Revisit if a reviewer asks.

### D5 — Importer test coverage {#d5}

`R/import_functs.R` is at 16.6%; ondisc-related paths are at 0%. Reviewers occasionally run `covr` and notice gaps.

**Decision:** deferred. Shape-only smoke tests were drafted but not landed; fixture-pinned dimensions (asserting against known truths read directly from the bundled `.mtx` files) would be stronger and could be added in a release-coordinated effort.

### D6 — `_v2` / `_v3` / `_v4` naming in the public C++ API {#d6}

Several functions in the public C++ API carry version-suffix names (`run_low_level_test_full_v4`, `compute_nt_nonzero_matrix_and_n_ok_pairs_v3`, `sample_undercover_pairs_v2`, …).

**Decision:** deferred. Not BiocCheck-flagged; reviewer-style item. Not pursued now to keep the current C++ PR (#210) surface focused. Easy to land later as its own focused rename PR with deprecation aliases on the public symbols.

### D7 — Polish items not flagged by BiocCheck {#d7}

Three items that have surfaced in earlier passes but are not check-flagged today:

- `LazyDataCompression: xz` — `data/` is 1 MB, well under any size flag.
- Gzip `inst/extdata/parse_example/gene_mat.mtx` — `inst/` is 700 KB total, not size-flagged.
- Gate `crayon::red()` / `crayon::blue()` on `interactive()` — ANSI escape codes leak into pipeline / CI logs when run non-interactively.

**Decision:** deferred. None are check-flagged; address only if a real-user complaint surfaces or as part of an unrelated PR that touches the same code.
